title: Electronic structure, magnetic order and anisotropic magnetoresistance in $\mathbf{Eu_{1-x}Gd_xCd_2P_2}$ (0 $\le$ x $\le$1)
abstract: Recently, $\text{EuCd}_2\text{P}_2$ has attracted increased attention for its colossal magnetoresistive (CMR) property, the mechanism of which seems to deviate from that of known canonical CMR compounds such as manganites. Many studies underscore the role of low density of hole carriers caused by Eu vacancies, particularly in stabilizing ferromagnetic (FM) order and modifying electrical transport and magnetoresistive responses in this compound. A magnetic polaron based mechanism rather than double exchange based mechanism is being proposed to explain the CMR effect for this compound. In this work, we explore the effect of elctron doping on the magnetic transition and CMR behaviour via Gd substitution at Eu sites with varying concentration (x) in Eu$_{1-x}$Gd$_{x}$Cd$_2$P$_2$. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo-based calculations reveal an oscillating ground state magnetic order as a function of electron carrier density. The ground state is found to be A-AFM metal for x=0.056, 0.125 and 0.5 while it becomes ferromagnetic metal at x= 0.33, 0.67 and 1. Most importantly, we predict colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance in this compound for x=0.125 and 0.5. The underlying mechanism of anisotropic CMR in this compound looks similar to double exchange like due to the presence of a strong intra-site 4\textit{f}-5\textit{d} ferromagnetic exchange interaction and an itinerant electron in the hybridized conduction states. The oscillating ground state magnetic order and the enhancement of transition temperature (as high as 150K for x=0.67) as a function of electron carrier density offers a new avenue to tune the magnetotransport property in this compound and offers an excellent platform for designing future spintronics devices.
summary: This theoretical study uses DFT and Monte Carlo methods to map the magnetic and electronic phase diagram of $	ext{Eu}_{1-x}	ext{Gd}_x	ext{Cd}_2	ext{P}_2$ as a function of Gd doping. The authors find that the magnetic order oscillates between antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic states, leading to the prediction of colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance at specific doping levels. This work highlights the tunability of magnetotransport properties in these correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how electron doping, achieved via Gd substitution, affects the magnetic transition and Colossal Magnetoresistance (CMR) behavior in the $	ext{Eu}_{1-x}	ext{Gd}_x	ext{Cd}_2	ext{P}_2$ system.
main_result: The ground state magnetic order oscillates between A-AFM and FM as a function of doping concentration, and colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance is predicted for specific doping levels ($x=0.125$ and $x=0.5$).
method: The research employs Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, supplemented by Monte Carlo simulations on a Heisenberg spin model, to predict magnetic and electronic properties.
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered magnetic semiconductor $	ext{Eu}_{1-x}	ext{Gd}_x	ext{Cd}_2	ext{P}_2$. Gd substitution acts as an electron dopant, modifying the magnetic exchange interactions and electronic character.
key_observables: Ground state magnetic order (A-AFM vs. FM), Colossal Anisotropic Magnetoresistance (AMR), magnetic transition temperature ($T_C$), and band gap.
important_parameters: Doping concentration $x$ (ranging from 0 to 1), and the electron carrier density.
main_assumptions: The calculations utilize $	ext{GGA}+	ext{U}$ and $	ext{GGA}+	ext{U}+	ext{SO}$ approximations, and the mechanism is compared to double exchange, suggesting strong $4f-5d$ exchange interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the electronic structure (DOS/Band structure) and the magnetic transition temperatures ($C_V$ vs. $T$) across different doping levels.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the magnetic ground state and electronic structure across the doping series ($x$). It first establishes the parent compound ($x=0$), then tracks the transition from A-AFM to FM, predicting AMR based on the change in electronic character (insulating vs. metallic) along specific crystallographic directions.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed theoretical map of how doping can tune magnetic order and transport properties in a strongly correlated material, offering insights into designing next-generation spintronic devices.
